question: For a parallel plate capacitor, the rate of change of electric field is doubled and the plate area is reduced to half. How will the displacement current change? Justify your answer.

options.A: $I_D'=\varepsilon_0\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\left(2\dfrac{dE}{dt}\right)=\varepsilon_0A\dfrac{dE}{dt}=I_D$. Hence the displacement current remains unchanged.
options.B: $I_D'$ doubles because the rate of change of electric field is doubled.
options.C: $I_D'$ becomes half because the plate area is halved.
options.D: $I_D'$ becomes one-fourth because area is halved and rate of change is doubled.
